changes.how: Step 0.13 made this file: a "use client" file importing only next/link and react, exporting `type LinkPolicy = "view" | "intent" | "none"` and PolicyLink, which keeps `const [asked, setAsked] = useState(false)` and renders `<Link {...rest} prefetch={policy === "view" || (policy === "intent" && asked) ? null : false} …>` with onPointerEnter, onTouchStart and onFocus each calling setAsked(true) and then the given handler. Rename the policies to the plan's words, which steps 2.7 and 2.8 use: `export type LinkPolicy = "sight" | "intent" | "never";` and `prefetch={policy === "sight" || (policy === "intent" && asked) ? null : false}`; in the doc comment 'view' becomes 'sight' and 'none' becomes 'never'. Change nothing else: the handlers, the props passed through (`scroll`, `replace`, `aria-current`, `hrefLang`, `lang`, `className`, `target`, `rel`) and the children stay as 0.13 wrote them. `prefetch={null}` is Next's default (fetch when in view); `false` fetches nothing.

changes.how: Step 0.12 made this file and step 1.3 left in it: a helper watch(page) returning { prefetches, stylesheets } (prefetches are the router's prefetch requests, by the headers named in its comment), a helper readToFooter(page), and a table ROUTER_REQUESTS: Record<string, number> with one test per row on the phone viewport (390 by 844, isMobile, hasTouch) that loads the page, calls readToFooter(page), waits until no router request has started for 3,000 ms and expects the count to be at most the row's budget (E2E_MEASURE=1 prints it instead). A router request here is an entry of watch(page).prefetches. In ROUTER_REQUESTS set '/s/demo/no', '/s/demo/no/p/demo-keramikkopp' and '/s/demo/no/cart' to 6 and add the row '/s/demo/no/om-oss': 6 (a content page of the demo seed); leave the other rows as step 1.3 set them. Add a test 'the home on a computer fetches little ahead': viewport 1280 by 720, goto /s/demo/no, no scrolling, wait until no router request has started for 3,000 ms, expect watch(page).prefetches.length at most 8. Add the test `a footer link waits to be pointed at`: on the phone home, scroll to the footer, expect 0 router requests for /s/demo/no/cookies; hover (or focus) the cookies link, expect at least 1; press it and expect the address to change with no document request. Add `the first add to cart asks for little again`: phone, top of /s/demo/no/p/demo-handlenett, count router requests in the 4 s after the first press of Add to cart: at most 10 (32 before); after a second press: 0. Keep the comment that a change which passes a budget is a regression to look at, not a number to raise.

Add a section `## What the router fetches ahead` with this table. sight: the cart link on phones, a header menu's top links, product tiles (bounded by step 2.8), the site's sign-up button. intent: the logo, search, account, wishlist, the bottom bar's home and account, footers (menu, cookies, withdrawal, legal pages), menu sub-links, the phone menu, every admin link (AdminLink). never: countries, languages and currencies, links that leave their root layout, file links, the cart link from 768 px (a plain anchor). Then two sentences: a link states its policy through PolicyLink or AdminLink and next/link is imported only by them (ratchet count directLinks); a server action that sets a cookie or revalidates makes the router ask again for every link in view, so the number of sight links is also the cost of every such action.

Add a short rule at the end, under the heading `## Links say what they may fetch ahead (bloat review step 2.6)`: the sentence about PolicyLink's three policies, that a new file may not import next/link (ratchet), and that the table lives in docs/performance.md. Add the same one-line rule to the admin frame's file in docs/rules/admin/ (docs/rules/admin/README.md says which file is the frame's), naming AdminLink. commits.title: A ratchet lets direct imports of next/link only fall

changes.how: Export `export const DIRECT_LINK = /from\s+["']next\/link["']/g;` and a list `LINK_WRAPPERS = ["src/components/policy-link.tsx", "src/components/block-link.tsx", "src/components/admin/ui/link.tsx"]`. In `ratchetCounts(root)` add `const directLinks = {};` and, inside the loop over files, `if (!LINK_WRAPPERS.includes(file) && count(text, DIRECT_LINK) > 0) directLinks[file] = 1;`. Return it with the others: `{ unknownCasts, anySuppressed, untypedReads, byIdWrites, directLinks }`. Update the comment at the top of the file to name the new count.

In the block that collects `raised`, add: `for (const file of Object.keys(now.directLinks)) if (!(before.directLinks ?? now.directLinks)[file]) raised.push(`${file}: imports next/link directly; use PolicyLink or AdminLink`);` (when the baseline has no `directLinks` yet, the first run writes it as things stand). Make sure the written JSON includes `directLinks`.
Do not edit by hand: run `node scripts/ratchet.mjs`. The diff must only add the `directLinks` map (about 395 files; 400 before this step's commits) and change no other number.

In the style of the first case (`adds no unchecked read...`) add `adds no direct import of next/link: a file not in the baseline imports it not at all (use PolicyLink or AdminLink)`: every key of `ratchetCounts(root).directLinks` is a key of the baseline's `directLinks`. Extend the case `keeps the baseline as low as the code` so a file in the baseline's `directLinks` that no longer imports next/link fails with the message to run `node scripts/ratchet.mjs`. In `counts what it says it counts` add one line: `DIRECT_LINK` matches `import Link from "next/link";` and does not match `import { PolicyLink } from "./policy-link";`.
